body.statement: There exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \((\ell,u)\), such that \[cL_{n,B}\le\Psi^{\le}_{n,B}\le CL_{n,B}\] uniformly over feasible \((n,B)\). Hence \(\Psi_\infty(n)\asymp(\log n)/n\), and for every sufficiently large fixed \(A\), \(B_{\mathrm{sat}}(n,A)\asymp\log n\). In contrast, when \(n=4B\) and the box contains \((\sigma_1,\sigma_0)=(2,1)\), \(\Psi^{=}_{n,B}\ge1/3\), so compulsory overscheduling is separated from the at-most-\(B\) envelope.
body.justification: The result distinguishes the monotone operational budget from the nonmonotone mathematical cost of requiring many positive exact-count batches.
body.gap: Low-switching Neyman designs and batched-bandit results show that few updates can suffice, but they let surplus batches be ignored and do not exhibit an exact-count overscheduling penalty.
body.consumer: The Amazon adaptive-abtester consumer obtains both a stopping scale for useful revisions and a warning against mechanically forcing every available update slot to be used.
